name: QUDORA Technologies
description: QUDORA Technologies is a German full-stack quantum computing company building trapped-ion quantum computers and stand-alone ion-trap processors on its proprietary NFQC technology. It is a spin-off of the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), TU Braunschweig and Leibniz Universität Hannover, part of the Quantum Valley Lower Saxony ecosystem, and leads the federally funded NFQC-1k consortium aiming at a fault-tolerant trapped-ion system with at least 1,000 physical qubits.

news.title: QUDORA and ParityQC partner on algorithm optimization for trapped ions
news.excerpt: The partnership applies ParityQC's architecture to QUDORA's trapped-ion hardware to reduce gate counts and circuit depth.

news.title: QUDORA integrates NVIDIA CUDA-Q into Qamelion emulator and launches German-funded QUANDA HPC consortium
news.excerpt: QUDORA added NVIDIA CUDA-Q support to its SDK (qudora-sdk[cudaq]) so hybrid quantum-classical programs can run on its Qamelion emulator, which models trapped-ion noise, via QUDORA Cloud. It also launched QUANDA, a three-year project funded by Germany's BMFTR with partners including GWDG, Leibniz University Hannover and Deggendorf Institute of Technology, to integrate trapped-ion quantum computers into HPC centres and test quantum machine learning on energy-sector anomaly detection workloads. No funding amount was disclosed.

news.title: QUDORA joins EuroHPC Quantum Grand Challenge with Near Field Quantum Control project
news.excerpt: QUDORA is one of 13 European companies selected from 30 proposals in the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking's Quantum Grand Challenge. Its NEQTAR project is to set out a technical and financial path for scaling its Near Field Quantum Control technology alongside European supercomputing infrastructure; Phase 2 from January 2027 allows applications to the EIB Venture Debt Platform.
